tei:div.tei:p:
For the conductor of the Choir, a Psalm by David: The heavens tell of the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hand. Day utters speech to day and night to night expresses knowledge. There is neither speech nor words without their sound being heard. Their line goes out over the whole earth and at the ends of the world are their words, for the sun has He set a tent among them. And he (the sun) comes forth like a bridegroom from his canopy, rejoices like a hero to run a course. At one end of the heavens is his starting point and his circuit goes round to the other end — nothing can hide from his glow. The Torah of the Lord is flawless, refreshing the soul, the testimony of the Lord is faithful making the simple wise. The precepts of the Lord are upright, causing the heart to rejoice, the commandment of the Lord is clear, giving light to the eyes. The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring for ever, the judgments of
the Lord are truth, together just, they are more precious than gold, even than an abundance of refined gold, and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb. Your servant, too, is careful about them, for keeping them there is great reward. As for errors, who understands, cleanse me from hidden sins. From the arrogant, too, keep away Thy servant — let them not rule over me; then will I be without fault and clear of grave offence. May the words of my mouth be pleasing and the meditation of my heart before Thee, O Lord my Rock and my Redeemer.
